div.head: VI Atr Prol.
div.ab: Þis syndan þa gerædnessa, þe Engla rædgifan gecuran ⁊ gecwædan ⁊ geornlice lærdan, þæt man scolde healdan.
Þis syndan þa gerædnessa þe Engla rædgifan gecuran ⁊ gecwædan ⁊ geornlice lærdan þæt man scolde healdan.
Þis syndan þa gerædnessa þe Engla rædgifan gecuran and gecwædan and geornlice lærdan, þæt man scolde healdan.
Prol. Dies sind die Satzungen, welche die [Staats]räthe der Engländer erkoren und erklärt und ernstlich angewiesen haben, dass sie gehalten werden sollen.
Prologue. These are the ordinances which the councillors [of state] of the English have chosen and declared and earnestly instructed are to be kept.
These are the ordinances which the councillors of England have decided and agreed upon, earnestly enjoining that they should be observed.
These are the decrees which the councilors of the English determined upon, pronounced, and solemnly ordered to be obeyed.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
Manuscripts: K = London, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii, fols. 35v–37r.

Synonym for witan; see that word in Gl 1 ll. 5. 10; Introduction 14f.
conoperante bisheriger Texte war falsche Lesung. Ducange kennt concrepare für consentire. Nur hier ist, unzweifelhaft richtig, Æthelreds Name erwähnt; s. o. Einl. 13
conoperante of previous texts was a false reading. Ducange knows concrepare for consentire. Only here is Æthelred’s name mentioned, undoubtedly correctly; see above Introduction 13
Cf. rædboran, rædwitan, BT. pp. 782, 784 s.v.

The preamble of the Latin paraphrase is noteworthy for the additional information it supplies: Quodam tempore contigit ut regis Aeþelredi edicto concrepante archipresulumque Aelfeahi et Wulfstani hortatu instigante, universi Anglorum optimates die sancto pentecosten ad locum ab indigenis Eanham nominatum acciti sunt convenire.
